newsitem.title: USA: Anaconda Nickel on target for start-up end 1998.
newsitem.headline: Anaconda Nickel on target for start-up end 1998.

text.p: Anaconda Nickel Limited said it has finalised cost figures for its Murrin Murrin laterite nickel and cobalt project in Australia, due on stream at the end of 1998.

Somerset Parker, Anaconda's marketing advisor, said Fluor Daniel has just confirmed that the capital cost of the open pit mine and pressure acid leach plant will be A$901 million with an operating cost of 61 cents per pound of nickel after cobalt credits.
The calculations are based on a US$3.50 per pound nickel and $12.50 per pound cobalt price, Parker told Metal Bulletin's Minor Metals seminar.
Production will start up in the final quarter of 1998 and reach maximum output a year later at 45,000 tonnes of nickel and 3,000 tonnes of cobalt with a project life of 30 years.
Product will be available for sale in the first quarter of 1999 and will be of high quality to compete with production from the Raglan and Voisey's Bay projects.

Glencore International AG of Switzerland has exclusive rights to sell the cobalt and nickel. Glencore has a 40 percent stake in Murrin Murrin, and a 19 percent stake in Anaconda Nickel Limited, Parker said.
Anaconda is already working on studies to expand production.
"Our current plan is that we will approve the go-ahead for expansion to 75,000 tonnes of nickel a year and 5,000 tonnes of cobalt once the base plant is commissioned," Parker said.
The expanded capacity would be in place before the year 2000 at a relatively low capital cost.

Parker said there was general agreement that the price of cobalt was set to decline over the next few years with supply shortages unlikely especially as much of the new supply will come from stable countries such as Australia and Canada.
But by 2005 the growth in cobalt consumption in batteries and other applications will keep the market in balance and the price of cobalt may strengthen, Parker added.
Parker said further reserves will be available within trucking distance of the present Murrin Murrin project.
